IMPERIAL PA RLIAMENT.
THURSDAY.

In the House of Commons on Thursday evening, Mr. Bryce, answering Sir E. A. Bartlett, said the discretion as to proceedings with regard to the dabez Balfour corn panies, rested with the Director of Public Prosecutions: who was acting, he understood, under the advice of the law officers. Sir E. GREY informed Sir C. Dilke that the French Ambassador had sent a note stating that France made full reserves in respect to the agreement between Her Majesty's Government and the King of the Belgians as representing the Congo State. _ _ . _

In reply to Mr. Field, Sir W. HARCOURT said no trace could be found of the Conversion of German spirit into so called Irish whisky at Bristol. Sir W. HARCOURT moved a resolution giving Govern- ment business priority during the rest of the session. He said he could give no information as to what measures the government intended to promote until the Finance Bill was passed through, but they would endeavour to satisfy the pledges they had given, and the expectations they had held out. Mr. BALFOUR said Le thought the Government should have limited their demand for time to the questions they meant to deal with. Mr. SETON- KARR moved an amendment providing that the resolu- tion giving the Government the whole time of the House should only come into eperation im four weeks' time. Mr.J. Redmond put in an appeal on behalf of the Irish measures, Mr. Chamberlain inquired what was go- ing to be done with the time of the House. Mr.J. Wilson asked for some assurance as to the Miners' Eight Hours Bill, and Sir G. 0. Morgan called for an indication of the intentions of the Government with respect to the Welsh Disestablishment Bill. Sir W. Harcourt could only repeat what he said in moving his resolution. At the suggestion of Mr. Balfour, Mr. Seton-Karr (with the consent of the House) withdrew his amendment, and Mr. Goschen moved a new one to the effect that until the House was placed in possession of the views of the Government as to the course of publie businees no addi- tional facilities should be granted for the discussion of Government measures except financial business. After further discussion the amendment was rejected by 258 to 233, and the Government resolution was carried by 234 to 217. The House again went into Committee on the Budget

Bill. Mr. JEFFREYS moved an amendment that -the estate duty should be paid on all personal property. A good deal of talk on the amendment was indulged in, and Mr. Balfour was among the speakers. The amend- ment was negatived without a division. Mr. BUTCHER moved an amendment restricting the estate duty to pro- perty in this country. This amendment too was nega- tived without a division. Progress was reported at half- past twelve, after a protest against the manner in which the Opposition were obstructing business.

div.head: WIDNES RUGBY FOOTBALL CLUB.
div.p: WIDNES RUGBY FOOTBALL CLUB.
ANNUAL MEETING.

The annual general meeting of the Widnes Rugby Football Club, was held on Tuesday night at the Conservative Club Hall. Mr. H. Wade Deacon, J.P.. C.C., presided, and there was a large attendance of members.
REPORT AND BALANCE SHEET.

The report showed that during the past season the first team had played 37 matches, of which they had w,)ri 16, drawn 3, and lost 18, scoring 28 goals, 38 tries (243 points), against their opponents 21 goals, 22 tries (163 points). The "A " team had played 29 matches, of which they had won 20, drawn 5, and lost 4, scoring 30 goals, 55 tries (311 points), against 3 goals, 16 tries (63 points). The balance sheet stated that the income for the pabt season (including a balance of £2B 34. from the previous season) amounted to £575 163. 6.1. , Amongst the items of income were :—Gate money, first team, £370 7s. 7d.; "A "team, £57 Bs. 2 1; and inter- works matches, £62 12s. 9d.; members' subscript ions and donations, £55 11. s. 6d. The expenditure wls £572 83. 3d., leaving a balance in hand of £3 Eli. report and balance sheet were adopted on the motion of Mr. F. W. Wright and Mr. J. H. Smith.
ELECTION OF OFFICERS.

Mr. 11. Wade Deacon, J.P., C.C., was unanimously re-elected president. Tiao vice-presidents were re-elected with the addition of Mr. Stuart Deacon, 8.L., and Mr. J. S. Gilliat, M.P., to the list.—Mr. J. Drummond was elected captain of the first team and Mr. H. Barber sub- captain'. Mr. H. Peters was elected captain and Mr. W. Owens sub-captain cf the "A" team. Mr. F. W. Wright was re-elected hon. treasurer and Mr. F. Younge secretary. Mr. J. C. Evans was elected hon. assistant secretary. The following were elected to serve on the committee :—Messrs. J. IL Smith, T. Laws, T. Bold, F. Smith, E. Gordon, P. Dawson, J. E. Farrell, A. Critchley, and J. Roberts.

div.head: REDUCTION OF PLAYING MEMBERS ENTRANCE FZH.
div.p: REDUCTION OF PLAYING MEMBERS ENTRANCE FZH.

Mr. D. C. Alford proposed that the subscription for playing members, who have played in eight matches be 2;, only. He thought that there should be a differegce in the subscription of playing members, who had to stand all the hard knocks, and the members who stood amongst the spectator.. Mr. F. W. Wright seconded and the motion was carried unanimously.

div.head: TOTES OF THANKS.
div.p: TOTES OF THANKS.

A vote of thanks to the Press for their services during qhe year was moved by Mr. J. Roberts and carried.—Mr. J. H. Smith proposed a vote of thanks to tlieir President for presiding that evening. He was a good president and one who was not only ornamental but useful. He was always willing to come amongst them .—This motion was carried amid great applause.—The Chairman, in replying, after referring to the amicable way in which the meeting had been carried on, said lie could not help being struck with the remarkable success of the " A " team, and he had no doubt that a great deal was owing to Mr. F. W. Wright, who had captained the team. He was much obliged for the vote of thanks.
WARRINGTON WORKINGMEN'S PERMANENT BENEFIT BUILDING SOCIETY.

div.head: ANNUAL MEETING.
div.p: ANNUAL MEETING.

The annual general meeting of the members of the above society. was held on Monday evening in Golborne-st. (Baptist) schoolroom, the chair being occupied by Mr. J.W.Bouchier,one of the managers. There was a good attendance ef members. Amongst those present were—Managers, Messrs. James Harding, E. Wallington, Edward Fenton, Robert Isherwood, J. Baxter, George Armstrong, T. L. Woods, Henry Williamson, John Williamson, A. Walsh, and W. H. Wallington Mr. John Hatton (trustee), Mr. Josiah Longland (solicitor to the society), Mr. Peter Dalton (secretary), Mr. Joseph Potter, Mr. Greeley, and Mr. Ashley. The CHAIRMAN, in opening the proceedings, said that although the report might not be so satisfactory as some might wish, he thought that, considering the year they hsd passed through, the result was fairly satisfactory. (Hear, hear.) The SECRETARY read the annual report (the 24th) and the balance sheet. The report was as follows :—The tuin of £1,020 16s. Bd. has been received as sub;cript ions during the year,and £2,837 16s. for repayments, making the total receipts £3,858 12s. Bd. The with Ira wals dur- ing the year amounted to £1.642 Os. sd. tha sum of £1,129 63. 61. has been advanced to members during the year. There are 206 subscribers holdin,.• 295 shares, and 35 borrowers holding 176 shares, makina 241 mem- bers holding 471 shares. The profits for the year, in- eluding £l6B lls, from the last account, after deduct- ing working expenses, amount to £371 54. id., out of which the managers recommended a dividend of 4 per cent., which will take £371 Os. Ild. leaving a b dance of 4s. 21., which will be carried fcrward to next year's account. The reserve fund amounts to £5OO and the contingent fund to £2OO. The whole of the managers retire. Messrs. Harding,Wallington Fenton, Isherwood, Bouchier, and Baxter are eligible and offer VI, mselves for re-election. Six additional managers will be taken from the register in rotation. On the motion of the Chair- man seconded by Mr. R. Isherwood, the report was adopted. Mr. FENTON then moved—" That a dividend at the rate of four per cent, be paid investors on their de- posits." Mr. W. H. WALLINGTON seconded, and re- marked that the manner in which the society was conducted was a credit, not only to the managers, but to the town to which they belonged. This proposition was also carried.—On the motion of Mr. Harrott, seconded by Mr. ASHLEY, the retiring managers were re- elected.—Mr. JOSEPH Porrxn moved that Messrs. J. E. Wright and Wiliiam Bodle, jun., be re-elected surveyors for the ensuing year. This was seconded by Mr. GREELEY, and carried.—Mr. EDWARD WALLINGTON, in moving the election of Messrs. Samuel A Ibinson and George Armstrong as auditors, Mr. Armstrong taking the place of Mr. Ford resigned, said they might make the society better known, and draw a great number of mem- bers to bring in monev,but if there was not a correspond- ing number of purchasers they would be in a fix—Mr. FENTON seconded the motion, and said the difficulty pointed out by Mr. Wallington was provided for in the rules.—The motion was carried, and some formal busi- ness having been transacted the proceedings terminated with a vote of thanks to Mr. Bouchier for presiding.

div.head: SUCCESS OF WIDNESIAN ATHLETES.
div.p: SUCCESS OF WIDNESIAN ATHLETES.

At Southport Sports on Saturday, the following a Hl- letes from Widnes succeeded in winning prizes :-120 yards, H. Peters, first prize; mile handicap, E. Gordon, first prize ; and five miles scratch bicycle rart(, (N C.U. championship, Liverpool centre), D. Daglisb, first prize.

Herr Diiwe seems to have found a formidable cotupe tor in Mr. Hiram S. Maxim. The inventor of the famous gun which bears his name has produced a cuirass whhh he claims to be of less weight than that of lJ ve, and equally effectual, and the secret of which he offrrs for the sum of " 7s. 61. cash"! It is to he tested publicly at the Erith Gun Works to-day, and all interested are invited to witness the experiments. Mr. Maxim says the invention was projected and completed in one after- noon.

IS MARRIAGE A FAILURE? What a question to ask, but how often could it be answered in the affirmative the principal cause being the improvidence of Furnishing on the Hire System. Since our advertisements have appeared pointing out the disadvantages, we have re- ceived several le ters agreeing with our denunciations of this pernicious sys em. Each Hire Agreement specifies that after the deposit is paid, so many w-elfly payments shall be made and that until the whole of the sum mentioned is paid the goods shall not become the property of the would-be pur- chaser, and that if any of the payments are negh-cted to the exact time specified the goods may be forcibly taken away and the whole of the paym, nts forfeited. County Court judges have denounced the sy tern, inasmuch as the vender I gets both money and goods. Again, the pri es charged are enormous, without any respect being paid to the quality, in many cases being won c out before they are paid for. To com- bat this system, and open the eyes of the public, Worsley's of "The Pantheon," Gaythorn, Manchester, the Largest Retailers of Second-hand Furniture in the worlol, have determined to ailow all respectable householders to have furniture at the ticketed marked cash price, a small percentage being charged for the conven ence of payment by the week, month, or quarter. On the fourth page of the "Examiner" we advertise a list of Bargains every week, any of which can be had and paid for by convenient intervals, the articles being delivered upon the first payment being made. Furniture from £5 to £1 000 may be arrang,-id for in this way. To give an idea of the equity of our proposals we are prepared to , supply for a working man a House of Furniture complete, thoroughly gcod and suhstantial (every articli warranted), price £2O cash down, not a penny less, or 10 per cent extra if credit is given, making £22. Full particulars sent on application. GRE tT BARGAINS AT WORSLEY'S. ONE HUNDRED BEDROOM SUITES ON VIEW. The lowest ticketed price may be all very well in ribbons and lace, but this will not prove a good investment when appliedto furniture, the lowest priced furniture is not the cheapest by any means. The East End of London is swarming with Jews. Nearly 100,000 cabinet makers are manufacturing cheap furniture, showily veneered aril glazed with varnish, these arelsent to the Pro- vinces and retailed at window-ticketed-prices by drapers who wish to sell everything and dabble in every trade. Furniture Is usually purchased with an idea that it is to last for a life- time, and undoubtedly this is exactly what it should do. "The Pantheon," Gaythorn, is filled ts, overflowing with Second-hdnd Furniture, by good old makers, which can be sold at even less cot than the new flimsy rubbish from East London. Gillows, Ogden, ttc ,can be hid•for even less, which after renovations has the exact appearancs of new.
